chapter: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
title: The Rinkers and Crosbys in Spokane; Ma Bailey starts Mildred singing
summary: Al and Bing had a band in Spokane; Mildred left, married a man named Bailey and was pushed into singing by his mother, then worked San Francisco's Barbary Coast.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now the way Al and Bing I understand -- they lived -- they had a band together in Spokane.
In fact Al showed me a picture of the band with Bing playing drums and him playing piano, and --
And -- an old picture when I was up there.
And so they lived across the street the Rinkers and the Crosbys --
And that's where they got to --
-- and then Mildred left and that's when she married a fella named Bailey.
-- Ma Bailey's the one that started her singing.
Yeah, she started her singing. And --
But just encouraged her to sing, huh?
In fact she sent her out club shopped around and made her -- she was back stage in a closet, she said, go on, now, you go out and sing.
And she heard her sing around like this at the house, things like that.
No. No. I don't know what he does, because they went down to San Francisco and she worked down on the Barbary Coast with Tommy Lyman and all those people for a long while.
